sentences.text: Miadanasuchus was an extinct reptile belonging to the peirosaurid notosuchians that lived in Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous.
This animal reached an estimated length of 3 meters and possessed teeth that were irregularly spaced and varied in height.
The species was first described as Trematochampsa oblita by Éric Buffetaut and Philippe Taquet in 1979 based on fossils from the Maevarano Formation.
Additional material of the species was discovered since 1993 in the Miadana Hills near the village of Berivotra.
Miadanasuchus belongs to the parent group Peirosauridae and is classified in the family Peirosauridae.
Miadanasuchus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Fossils found in the Ankazomihaboka Formation potentially extend the species' temporal range back to the Coniacian.
